answer: A new agent should earn trust through work rather than names. Each entrant locks 40 tokens, draws a random task, signs its result, and gets three reviews from established peers; an auditor replays a sample. Passing returns the bond and builds reputation; copied proofs forfeit it and suspend keys for 12 rounds. A farm of 700 accounts ties up 28,000 tokens and pays for 2,100 reviews before claiming rewards. A public hash log exposes reuse: a fake swarm can ripple across the network, but each identity must climb the same costly ridge, while one genuine voyage leaves its own verifiable trail.
